comment: Identity defaults: what a profile with no keys of its own in a model group, and no deviceModelFrom, takes from its identity. Each entry is written from the gate it replaces in the code of 9bd6279, and its match names no more than that gate tested. The first entry that matches wins. No catalog profile takes a group from here: each carries its own keys, names its model or has nothing in the group, and switch-pro, switch-pro-usb and dualshock-3-full are their own identities' models. A profile made outside the catalog, by HMProfileBuilder, by HMDeviceExtractor or in a user's JSON, keeps through these entries the behavior its identity got from that code.

entries.name: nintendo-switch-pro-usb
entries.comment: The Switch Pro Controller on USB, 057E:2009: the same gate, with the protocol of the pad's USB descriptor, whose reports the Bluetooth protocol does not fit.

entries.name: nintendo-switch-pro
entries.comment: The Switch Pro Controller, 057E:2009: the protocol responder, packer and rumble decode gated on that pair (SwitchProPacker.IsSwitchPro and driver.c's ReadConfigFromRegistry at 9bd6279).

entries.name: sony-sixaxis
entries.comment: A DualShock 3 in the sixaxis form, gated on the sixaxisCompatible key (the Ds3Sixaxis value the driver read at 9bd6279).

entries.name: sony-dualshock4-bt
entries.comment: Sony's feature answers, the DualShock 4 branch: report 0x05's DualShock 4 order for 05C4, 09CC and 0BA0, with the Bluetooth CRC for a Bluetooth profile (driver.c's Sony table at 9bd6279, gated on VID 054C).

entries.name: sony-dualshock4
entries.comment: The same over USB, no CRC.

entries.name: sony-dualsense-edge-bt
entries.comment: Sony's feature answers, the Edge branch: report 0x20's firmware line for 0DF2, with the Bluetooth CRC.

entries.name: sony-dualsense-edge
entries.comment: The same over USB, no CRC.

entries.name: sony-dualsense-bt
entries.comment: Sony's feature answers for every other Sony PID, the DualSense default, with the Bluetooth CRC.

entries.name: sony-dualsense
entries.comment: The same over USB, no CRC.

entries.name: microsoft-xbox-named
entries.comment: An XUSB companion beside the HID device, the presentation of xbox-360-wired, for a Microsoft profile with xbox in its id, name or product string. The SDK made the companion for VID 045E with xbox in one of those three, unless the profile bound xinputhid (ControllerProfile.RequiresXusbCompanion at 9bd6279). A profile with driverMode xinputhid or xusb22 states its presentation itself, so the entry fills nothing for it. Windows names the HID children of XInput devices itself, Controller (XBOX 360 For Windows) for 028E, 028F and 0719 and Controller (Xbox One For Windows) for the Xbox One and Series PIDs (Wine dlls/hidclass.sys/device.c:379-393 at 2df1ee2), so a pad extracted on Windows matches.
